Show what will be posted
     
    Round I · while coding
    Implementation assumptions
    Where the ticket was ambiguous: the reading the coder chose.
    1. assumption50% confident No index added for the date sort
      Read the other way: a Flyway migration indexing visits(visit_date, id)
      Why 50%: The seed has 28 visits and the ticket does not mention scale. If volume grows, sorting the whole table per page will show up, so this is a coin flip on when.
      VisitRepository.java
      

      2. 

    2. assumption60% confident Ties within a sorted column fall back to latest first, then id
      Read the other way: tie-break by id only, as the owners grid does
      Why 60%: When one pet has several visits, showing them chronologically is the useful order, and the id still makes paging stable. Nobody asked for it, so a plain id tie-break is equally defensible.
      

      3. 

    3. assumption65% confident API caps the page size at 100, not at the three UI sizes
      Read the other way: reject any size other than 5, 10 or 20 in the API too
      Why 65%: It copies the owners endpoint (MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100), and the ticket describes the grid, not the API. A stricter reading of "5, 10, or 20" would hold the API to it too.
      VisitRestController.java
      

      4. 

    4. assumption70% confident Paging runs on the server, not in the browser
      Read the other way: keep the bare list; page and sort client-side with MatTableDataSource
      Why 70%: The owners grid (#25) paged on the server, and visits grow without bound. The ticket says only "paginated", and the browser-side version needed no API break, which pulls this down.
      VisitRepository.java
      

      5. 

    5. assumption75% confident Owner column sorts by first name, then last name
      Read the other way: sort by last name, as a clinic register usually does
      Why 75%: The cell reads "First Last", so this sort matches what is shown, and owners' Name sort does the same. A clinic looking people up by surname would want last name first.
      

      6. 

    6. assumption90% confident Default view is the 10 latest visits
      Read the other way: the first page in id or ascending-date order
      Why 90%: The grid already sorted newest first before paging, so this keeps what users saw. Ten is the middle of the three sizes the ticket names.
      

    Round II · code review
    Open review issues
    Left in the code, each with its reason. They stay open until you agree or disagree.
    1. nitsecurity reviewer Page index has no upper bound
      Reviewer: page=2000000000&size=100 makes the database run a huge OFFSET plus a count on every call.
      endpoint is admin-only; OFFSET past the end stops at table size. Same as owners paging.
      VisitRestController.java
      

      2. 

    2. nitticket-fit reviewer API accepts sizes 1..100, not only 5/10/20
      Reviewer: the ticket names 5, 10 and 20 rows, yet ?size=7 or ?size=100 is served. The UI quietly resets an unsupported URL size to 10.
      the ticket constrains the grid; the API serves other clients. Recorded under Assumptions.
      VisitRestController.java
      

      3. 

    3. nitcorrectness reviewer Past-the-end redirect could loop or show stale rows
      Reviewer: when the last page empties after deletes, show() navigates to totalPages. If the data shifts again it re-navigates while the old rows stay on screen.
      each redirect needs a fresh empty answer; it converges as soon as deletes stop.
      visits-page.component.ts
      

      4. 

    4. nittests reviewer Pet and owner sort direction and tie-breaks not pinned
      Reviewer: the pet sort is tested ascending only and the owner sort descending only, so flipping direction there would stay green.
      one shared direction variable; asc and desc both pinned for description, owner tie-break pinned.
      VisitListTest.java
      

      5. 

    5. nittests reviewer Query-count bound of 3 is loose
      Reviewer: isLessThanOrEqualTo(3) would still pass with one extra lazy load if the count query were skipped.
      an N+1 regression over 20 rows needs 20+ statements; the bound catches that.
      

      6. 

    6. nittests reviewer Frontend specs stub the router, so the URL round trip is unproven
      Reviewer: Router.navigate is stubbed and ActivatedRoute faked, so a real routing bug would pass every unit test.
      Playwright drives the real round trip: header click and next page (visits.spec.ts:49, 61).
      

      7. 

    7. nittests reviewer Removed getAll tests thin seed-data and role coverage
      Reviewer: no test checks that the list still returns seeded rows, or that a non-admin gets a 403.
      class-level @PreAuthorize is unchanged; Playwright compares the grid to the seeded API page.
      

      8. 

    8. contextcorrectness reviewer Text sort order depends on database collation
      Reviewer: mixed-case descriptions or pet names ("abc", "Zed") may sort differently on H2 and on Postgres.
      Postgres is the only database here (dev and tests); there is no H2 in the project.
      VisitRestController.java
      

      9. 

    9. contexttests reviewer Uppercase or malformed sort values untested
      Reviewer: sort=date,ASC, sort=date,asc,extra and page=abc are never tested, and the uppercase form is rejected.
      the 400 on anything off-pattern is intended and pinned by unsupportedSortKey_isRejected.
      VisitListTest.java
